# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 packets, 2024-08-15 04:09:43–04:42:26 UTC). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory; all findings below are derived directly from packet capture analysis with tshark.

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **plucero** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNames `plucero` and `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` against DC 10.8.15.4 / WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) |

Host identity was cross-confirmed via DHCP (option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` from MAC `00:1c:bf:03:54:82`), NBNS name registrations, and ARP resolution (10.8.15.133 → same MAC).

## 2. Malware Family

**Latrodectus** loader/downloader malware. **Attribution is behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — the evidence set contains no AV/EDR alert or YARA match; the call is based on the following distinctive, observed TTP chain matching known Latrodectus behavior:

- Fake shipping-invoice lure (FedEx-themed) delivering a heavily junk-padded ZIP → oversized obfuscated `.js` downloader (~7 MB of decoy text hiding a small amount of real WScript logic, including a `WScript.Sleep(10000)` evasion call).
- JS downloader phones home to a `checkfedexexp[.]com` tracking/gate endpoint before fetching the next stage.
- Next-stage payload is a Windows PE32+ DLL fetched via **BITS** (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` User-Agent) directly to a bare IP address (no DNS lookup for the C2 host — DNS-avoidance behavior).
- Payload DLL's internal name is `release.dll`, exporting `DllRegisterServer` / `DllGetClassObject` / `DllUnregisterServer` / `Start` — consistent with regsvr32/rundll32-style DLL loaders used by Latrodectus.
- Post-execution, the host beacons persistently over plain HTTP to the same bare-IP host, sending a fixed ~230-byte Base64-style blob in the `Cookie` header on every request, spoofing an obsolete `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` browser User-Agent — a known Latrodectus C2 check-in signature.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

### Malicious domains
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 104.21.55.70, Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 104.21.55.70, Cloudflare-fronted)

### Malicious URLs
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — GET at T+74.7s, delivered the malicious ZIP (`data-text-lines`/zip content, 2.77 MB response)
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent=...` — gate/tracking URL hardcoded inside the JS downloader

### Command-and-control
- **72.5.43.29:80/tcp** — raw-IP HTTP C2 (no DNS resolution observed for this host)
  - `HEAD /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` and `GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` at T+135.9s via BITS — payload retrieval
  - Sustained beaconing from T+196.9s through end of capture: repeated `GET /` and `POST /` with `User-Agent: Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` and a static Base64-style `Cookie` value (`1dPYCLQThlalsevmZ8Gm4HAmczKbbrMbgfmn54P1NiJU+...`), 304 GET / 3 POST / 1 HEAD requests total, mostly answered `HTTP 400`

### Transferred files and hashes
| File | SHA-256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `managements?...` (delivered ZIP) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Downloaded from quote.checkfedexexp.com |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | 6,990,020 bytes, extracted from ZIP; junk-padded JScript downloader containing `WScript.Sleep(10000)` and a hardcoded call to `business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | 159,232-byte PE32+ x86-64 DLL, internal name `release.dll`, exports `DllRegisterServer`/`DllGetClassObject`/`DllUnregisterServer`/`Start`; fetched via BITS from `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` |

## 4. Attack Timeline (relative to capture start)

| T+ (s) | Event |
|---|---|
| 74.7 | GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` — malicious ZIP delivered |
| ~135.9–136.9 | BITS HEAD/GET pulls `release.dll` payload from `72.5.43.29` |
| 196.9 onward | Persistent HTTP beaconing (GET/POST `/` with fixed Cookie + spoofed IE6 UA) to `72.5.43.29:80`, continuing through end of capture (T+1962s) |

**Recommended containment:** isolate 10.8.15.133, block egress to 72.5.43.29 and `*.checkfedexexp.com`, reset credentials for `plucero`, and forensically image the host to recover on-disk artifacts (dropped `release.dll`, execution mechanism, and persistence) since this pcap alone does not show the exact process-execution method (regsvr32/rundll32/schtasks).
